findings.title: Snapshot progress can be overwritten by a stale INCONSISTENCY reply
findings.scenario: RG3 snapshot race / old append reply after snapshot progress
findings.summary: After the repair pass, the remaining current violation is that a follower can generate an INCONSISTENCY reply before snapshot progress is recorded, and the leader can receive that reply after SnapshotInstalled has raised matchIndex, snapshotIndex, and nextIndex. The normal INCONSISTENCY branch still computes a lower nextIndex with LogAppenderBase.getNextIndexForInconsistency and calls FollowerInfoImpl.setNextIndex. This can move nextIndex below the proven snapshot boundary, causing the leader to lose recorded replication progress and retry work below the installed snapshot.

findings.title: Staging appender restart discards proven catch-up progress
findings.summary: A staging peer can reach the catch-up boundary through snapshot progress, with matchIndex and snapshotIndex at ConfLogIndex and nextIndex advanced beyond it. LeaderStateImpl.restart removes the current appender and creates a new FollowerInfoImpl through addAndStartSenders instead of preserving the old follower progress fields. The replacement follower state resets matchIndex, snapshotIndex, nextIndex, and attemptedSnapshot, so the staging peer remains in staging but loses the progress needed for catch-up.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 3 (same staging appender restart and catch-up progress loss mechanism)

findings.title: Stream reconnect and late replies may lose pending-request context
findings.scenario: Scenario 1: Stream Reconnect, Late Replies, and Pending Request Reset
findings.summary: The gRPC appender stores each AppendEntries request in a pending map and optimistically advances nextIndex before the follower reply arrives. Stream reset clears pendingRequests and timeout removes an individual request, but the reply handler can still process a later success or inconsistency reply even when the original request context is absent. This scenario asks whether late, duplicate, or out-of-order replies after reconnect, reset, or timeout can reduce nextIndex below proven progress or otherwise corrupt follower progress state. The current MC candidates cover the snapshot-boundary race and staging restart race, but not the standalone stream reconnect and pending-request reset mechanism.

findings.title: Cancellation, backpressure, and stream resource boundaries may duplicate or retain work
findings.scenario: Scenario 4: Cancellation, Backpressure, and Resource Boundaries
findings.summary: AppendEntries sends wait for stream readiness, while snapshot streaming uses StreamObserverWithTimeout and server-side stream completion or error handling to bound outstanding work. The modeling brief raises cancellation, retry, and backpressure as a separate lifecycle mechanism that can amplify duplicate sends, retry loops, or retained per-stream state. This is mostly resource and hardening oriented rather than a compact Raft safety-state violation, but it is still a code-review scenario for confirmation. No current MC candidate covers cancellation cleanup, snapshot backpressure, or server-stream resource retention, so it remains a separate code-review candidate.
